source.title: Multi-Granular Node Pruning for Causal Circuit Discovery
source.authors: Muhammad Umair Haider; Hammad Rizwan; Hassan Sajjad; A. Siddique

record.file_problem: Minor PDF/OCR formatting artifacts; the text is readable and does not appear cut off.
record.tranche_reason: The study applies a different, node-mask circuit-discovery method to IOI and evaluates task performance in the resulting circuits; it also analyzes IOI circuitry in other models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports IOI results for its own pruned circuits and a qualitative head-role analysis for Llama 3.2-1B. It does not test backup-head takeover, and it does not compare selected component identities across discovery methods. Hyperparameter-sweep values and cited findings are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: A new node-pruning discovery method is applied to IOI in GPT-2 small. Its per-layer head retention (Table 6) can be checked against the original circuit's head locations, which bears on V4. A role analysis in Llama-3.2-1B bears on V3. Fidelity numbers are the method's own performance and do not test any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The main conclusion is that multi-granular node pruning finds more compact circuits with 3-11× less memory. They also say IOI is MLP-dominant with sparse late attention in GPT-2 and Llama, and that Llama-3.2-1B late heads show IO-Mover, S-Inhibitor and S-Promoter roles mirroring the GPT-2 circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The method learns hierarchical block, head, and neuron masks by interpolating clean and corrupted activations, rather than reproducing the original circuit's edge/head interventions and validation procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported sparsity coefficient λ sweep shows task performance and KL change with the sparsity setting; the paper states performance degrades sharply past λ = 0.975 for GPT-2 and approximately 0.85 for Llama-3.2-1B.

fits_no_version.finding: In IOI circuits from node pruning, MLP blocks stay active across most layers in GPT-2 small, both Llamas and GPT-2-XL, while attention is sparse and mostly in late layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI in these models depends on MLP computation distributed across depth, not only on attention heads.

record.problems: The paper's node masks identify retained components but do not recover their interaction structure, directionality, or multiplicity (stated in Limitations). The qualitative Llama head-role assignments rely on attention and attribution analyses rather than reported causal tests of each role.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI results for GPT-2 small were omitted from the included tables and layer summaries. Hyperparameter-sweep plots are not included because they do not test the specified ablation, prompt-distribution, or prompt-variant claims; non-IOI task results are outside the claim.

untested.parts: The original 26-head circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not evaluated directly.
No ablation of name movers; backup takeover is not tested.
No training checkpoints and no reuse of components across tasks. No role analysis for Llama-8B or GPT-2-XL.
Ablation type, metric and prompt distribution are not varied; only a λ sparsity sweep is run.
No results broken down by template, name order or number of names.

missing.what: Per-layer IOI head retention for the other methods on GPT-2 small: EP, EAP and DiscoGP. EP keeps heads in every layer; EAP keeps far more heads; EAP's IOI circuit has accuracy 0.000. This shows other methods recover very different head sets, which bears on V4.
Stability of the Llama-3.2-1B IOI head selection across 5 seeds (consistent).

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper. Fidelity rows are re-linked to none because they measure the method's own performance. The V4 comparison uses the original paper's head locations against the study's per-layer head counts in Table 6; the study itself makes no such comparison. The study's corruption scheme and KL+margin objective differ from the original's path patching.

versions.untested_parts: It does not test the original 26-head, 7-class circuit or its individual head classes, nor the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria as defined in that work.
No main name-mover ablation or test of backup-head takeover.
No training-checkpoint comparisons or reuse of the components for other tasks; the named roles are analyzed qualitatively for Llama 3.2-1B, not established across every reported model.
The study compares pruning rates and fidelity across methods, but does not test whether other methods recover the same components or roles.
The study sweeps sparsity coefficient λ, but does not compare ablation types or prompt distributions to test the specified sensitivity claim.

Although its IOI dataset uses multiple templates, it does not report results separately by name order, template, or number of names, or test whether the same components carry behavior across variants.

rows.subject: Llama-3.2-1B
rows.operation_detail: Analyzes attention to IO and repeated-subject tokens and Direct Logit Attribution for surviving heads.
rows.baseline: not stated
rows.value: Reports IO-Movers, S-Inhibitors, and S-Promoters; authors say the pattern mirrors roles identified in the manually discovered GPT-2 IOI circuit.
rows.note: Role assignment is based on attention and attribution analyses, not a reported causal patching test of each role.
rows.check: Only late-layer mover-like and inhibitor-like roles are found, by attention and DLA alone. Attention in layers 0-7 is almost entirely pruned, so no duplicate, induction or previous-token classes appear. Here 'S-Inhibitors' means direct negative-DLA heads, not the original's query-composition role.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small IOI, node-pruning with clean/corrupted interpolation
relationships.reason: The recovered circuit keeps no heads in layers 2, 4, 6, 8 and 11, dropping the original's previous-token head 4.11, induction head 6.9, S-inhibition heads 8.6/8.10 and backup heads in layer 11. Head identities in the kept layers are unreported. This comparison against the original head list is ours, not the paper's (gpt2-layer-2, -4, -6, -8, -11, ioi-gpt2-structure).
relationships.display_finding: Comparison with the original circuit shows that excluding layers 2, 4, 6, 8, and 11 removed previous-token head 4.11, induction head 6.9, S-inhibition heads 8.6 and 8.10, and layer-11 backup heads.

source_check.notes: Original GPT-2 head identities are supplied by the pack, not established by this paper. Table 2 reports 43.8% attention-block pruning for Llama-3.2-1B, whereas Table 15 lists nine of sixteen attention blocks as pruned.

statements.correction: Llama-3.2-1B: late-layer roles assigned using attention and DLA; complete original-class mapping and causal role tests unreported. Early attention mostly pruned, with two surviving heads in layer 2. Llama-3.1-8B and GPT-2-XL: topology reported without named head-role mappings.
statements.problem: The descriptive facts are supported, but their placement as limits_scope treats untested original classes as evidence of incomplete preservation.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: GPT-2 small, IOI, the study's learned node-pruned circuit
reader_labels.reason: The circuit retains strong task accuracy but has a different reported node-level structure, including substantial MLP retention; the results do not establish the original 26-head, seven-class mechanism or its criteria (ioi-gpt2-structure, ioi-gpt2-accuracy, ioi-gpt2-kl, ioi-gpt2-logit-difference, gpt2-layer-0 through gpt2-layer-11).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The pruned model retains strong IOI performance, and the qualitative analysis identifies IO-Mover and S-Inhibitor roles that the authors say mirror the GPT-2 IOI circuit (ioi-llama-1b-fidelity, ioi-llama-1b-roles).
